unit.unitOverview: Say and write the 26 letters. Read short words, sound by sound: b-u-s, bus. Learn ten working words: listen, look, say, write. Can you read bus, map and stop? Yes? Do Practice 6. Then go to Unit 1.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: tap, listen, repeat.
Patterns: letters, sounds, blending.
Read three short texts.
Speak. Record. Listen back.
Write letters and words.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
unit.origin: Compressed from Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1

visual.lectureScript:
Hello. This is Unit 0: Letters and Sounds.
First, a check. Read these words: bus, map, cup, stop.
Easy? Do Practice 6. Then go to Unit 1.
Not easy? Stay here. This unit is for you.
English has 26 letters.
Every letter has a name. Listen: a, b, c, d, e.
Every letter is capital or small.
This is capital B. This is small b.
Now, sounds.
Five letters are vowels: a, e, i, o, u.
In a short word, a vowel has a short sound.
Listen: bag. bed. sit. box. bus.
The other letters have a sound too.
Listen to the start of each word: bus, map, sun, pen, hat.
Two letters can make one sound.
s and h make sh: shop, fish.
c and h make ch: chin, chip.
t and h make th: this, that.
Now, reading.
Look at a word: bus.
Point to each letter. Say its sound, not its name.
Then say the sounds again, fast.
The sounds join. They make the word: bus.
That is reading. You can read cup, sun and stop like this.
Last, ten working words.
Listen. Look. Say. Read. Write.
Tap. Match. Point. Check. Repeat.
Every unit uses them. Learn them here.
Listen: use your ears. Look: use your eyes.
Now go to Words.
Tap a word. Listen. Say it. Repeat it.

grammar.title: The alphabet: 26 letters, A to Z
grammar.explanation:
English has 26 letters.
Every letter has a name.
Every letter is capital or small: B, b.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
A a   B b   C c   D d   E e   F f   G g
H h   I i   J j   K k   L l   M m   N n
O o   P p   Q q   R r   S s   T t   U u
V v   W w   X x   Y y   Z z

Capital:  B   M   S
Small:    b   m   s

Order:  a b c d e … x y z
grammar.workedExample:
Put in order: c, a, b.
1. Say the alphabet: a, b, c …
2. a is first. Write a.
3. Then b. Write b.
4. Then c. Write c.
Answer: a, b, c.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to mix b and d.
b: the line, then the circle.
d: the circle, then the line.
Check with the word bed.
grammar.memoryTip:
bed looks like a bed.
b is at one end. d is at the other.
grammar.practice:
1. Write the capital: a, g, m, r, e
2. Write the small letter: B, D, Q, T, H
3. Write the missing letter: a b _ d
4. Write the missing letter: l m _ o p
5. Put in order: d, b, c, a
6. Put in order: s, r, t
grammar.answerKey:
1. A, G, M, R, E
2. b, d, q, t, h
3. c
4. n
5. a, b, c, d
6. r, s, t
Check 2.
Is d written as b? Is q written as p?
Look at bed. Small q has a tail, like g.

grammar.title: Short vowel sounds: a, e, i, o, u
grammar.explanation:
Five letters are vowels: a, e, i, o, u.
In short words, they have a short sound.
Listen: bag, bed, sit, box, bus.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
a    bag   map   hat
e    bed   pen   leg   wet
i    sit   fix   bin
o    box   hot   stop
u    bus   cup   sun
grammar.workedExample:
Find the vowel in pen.
1. Look: p, e, n.
2. Which one is a, e, i, o or u? e.
3. Say pen. Listen to the middle.
4. It is the sound in bed.
Answer: e, as in bed.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to mix e and i.
pen is not pin. bed is not bid.
For e, open your mouth a little more.
grammar.memoryTip: a: bag. e: bed. i: sit. o: box. u: bus.
grammar.practice:
Say each word. Write its vowel: a, e, i, o or u.
1. map
2. wet
3. bin
4. hot
5. cup
6. leg
7. fix
8. sun
grammar.answerKey:
1. a
2. e
3. i
4. o
5. u
6. e
7. i
8. u
Check 2 and 6.
wet and leg have the e of bed.
They do not have the i of sit.

grammar.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
grammar.title: Consonant sounds, with sh, ch and th
grammar.explanation:
The other letters have a sound too.
Listen to the start: bus, map, sun.
Two letters can make one sound: sh, ch, th.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
b  bus     d  bed     f  fix     h  hat
l  leg     m  map     n  bin     p  pen
s  sun     t  tap     w  wet     c  cup (like k)
x  box  (two sounds: k s)

Two letters, one sound:
sh   shop   fish
ch   chin   chip
th   this   that
grammar.workedExample:
Find the first sound in shop.
1. Look: s, h, o, p.
2. s and h are together.
3. Together they make one sound: sh.
4. So shop has 3 sounds: sh, o, p.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to say s for sh.
sh is not s.
For sh, push your lips out: shop.
For s, lips back: sun.
grammar.memoryTip: Sh! Put a finger on your lips. That is the sound.
grammar.practice:
Two letters, one sound.
Write sh, ch or th.
1. shop
2. chin
3. this
4. fish
5. much
6. that
Now write the first letter.
7. bus
8. map
grammar.answerKey:
1. sh
2. ch
3. th
4. sh
5. ch
6. th
7. b
8. m
Check 4 and 5.
sh and ch can come last: fish, much.

grammar.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
grammar.title: Blending: join the sounds
grammar.explanation:
To read a new word, say each sound.
Then say the sounds again, fast.
They join and make the word.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
b - u - s        →  bus
c - u - p        →  cup
m - a - p        →  map
b - e - d        →  bed
s - i - t        →  sit
s - t - o - p    →  stop
sh - o - p       →  shop

Sounds. Join. Word.
grammar.workedExample:
Read h-o-t.
1. Point to h. Say its sound.
2. Point to o. Say its sound.
3. Point to t. Say its sound.
4. Say the three sounds again, fast.
5. They join: hot.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to say the names: b, u, s.
The names do not make bus.
Say the sounds. Then join them.
grammar.memoryTip: Point, say, join. Your finger goes left to right.
grammar.practice:
Say the sounds. Then say the word. Write it.
1. p-e-n
2. l-e-g
3. b-i-n
4. f-i-x
5. s-u-n
6. w-e-t
7. ch-i-n
8. s-t-o-p
grammar.answerKey:
1. pen
2. leg
3. bin
4. fix
5. sun
6. wet
7. chin
8. stop
Check 8.
Is there a sound between s and t? (sutop)
Keep s and t close: st-op, stop.

grammar.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
grammar.title: Ten working words: listen, look, say, write
grammar.explanation:
Every unit uses ten working words.
They tell you what to do.
Listen, look, say, read, write.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
👂  listen        👀  look
🗣️  say           📖  read
✍️  write         👆  tap
A ↔ a  match      👉  point
✅  check         🔁  repeat

Listen to the word.
Look at the word.
Say the word.
Repeat the word.
grammar.workedExample:
Read: Look. Point to b. Say it.
1. Look: use your eyes. Find b.
2. Point: put a finger on b.
3. Say: say b.
Three words, three things to do, in order.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to mix read and say.
Read: your eyes on the words.
Say: out loud, with your voice.
grammar.memoryTip: Listen: ears. Look: eyes. Say: mouth. Write: hand.
grammar.practice:
Match the word and the picture.
1. listen
2. look
3. write
4. point
5. say
6. check
a. 👉
b. 👂
c. ✅
d. 👀
e. 🗣️
f. ✍️
grammar.answerKey:
1. b
2. d
3. f
4. a
5. e
6. c
The likeliest slip is 1 and 2 swapped. Listen is ears 👂. Look is eyes 👀.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.note: The unit is built for a learner alone. Every pattern card has a worked example before its practice, every practice has an answer key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check. If you are helping, sit beside rather than lead: point to the line, let them press Listen, and let the key do the correcting.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.note: The narration voice reads a letter on its own by its NAME: b is heard as 'bee'. Where the page shows sounds one at a time (c - u - p, h-o-t), the learner should say the SOUND, which is the sound at the start of the word beside it (c as in cup). If you can, model the sounds yourself: short and clipped, with no added 'uh' (b, not 'buh'; s as a hiss, not 'suh'). This is the one place in the unit where a human voice adds something the recording cannot.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.note: A learner who already reads the Latin alphabet should not be held here. The overview and the first lines of the lesson ask them to read bus, map, cup and stop; if that is easy, they do Practice 6 (the ten working words every later instruction uses) and move to Unit 1. Check Practice 6 before they go — it is the one thing in this unit the rest of the course assumes.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.note: Reversing b and d, and p and q, is normal at this stage at any age and after any other script; the 'bed' shape in Pattern 1 is the quickest fix. Two sound slips to listen for: a vowel pushed in between two consonants (s-u-top for stop), and e and i merging (pen heard as pin). Both are in the answer keys, so the learner can find them without being told.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.note: Letters sit on a line, and g, j, p, q and y hang below it. Writing goes left to right. A learner used to a script that runs the other way may start at the right edge of the page — point to the left margin before they begin, and have them trace a finger along the line first. Any comfortable grip is fine; accuracy of shape matters more than speed.
